RustXNG

日本語 · 한국어

 
 
 
 
 
 

RustXNG is a self-hosted metasearch engine written in Rust, based on SearXNG. It combines results from external search providers and can fetch page text for AI agents through a JSON API or MCP.

RustXNG does not maintain a web-scale search index. You can add a local index of selected sites with rustxng-index and import Wikipedia dumps separately.

 Quick start

Install from the releases page or with Cargo. Release binaries are available for Linux, macOS and Windows; check the matching asset and its SHA-256 sidecar before running it.

 
 
 

Rust 1.89 or newer and a C build toolchain are required for source installation. The agent setup guide covers release binaries, verification, platform requirements and service reuse.

For automated clients that need errors for unknown engine names, add strict engines=1 (the default preserves SearXNG-compatible fallback behavior). Useful optional parameters include language=ja , engines=wikipedia , include domains=docs.rs , exclude domains=example.com , time range=day , and include raw content=1 . Time filtering depends on provider support.

The web interface is at . The search endpoint also supports CSV, RSS and HTML output.

 Use from an AI agent

If the agent is expected to install RustXNG itself, the agent setup guide is written for exactly that: it covers release-binary selection and checksum verification, starting a loopback service, verifying a small search, and the record to report back.

Start the built-in MCP server:

 

MCP exposes two read-only tools:

- search returns up to 10 ranked results. The default is 5, with snippets limited to 500 characters.
- read page retrieves text from a URL returned by search in the same session. It can return up to three passages relevant to an optional query , selected from the extracted page.

 read page returns 4,000 characters by default and allows max chars up to 20,000. Use offset and next offset to continue. truncated and source truncated indicate limits. MCP enforces serialized character and byte budgets. Supply both tokenizer ( cl100k base or o200k base ) and max payload tokens for an exact budget on serialized MCP structuredContent ; this does not include the JSON-RPC envelope or client/model framing. Output contract

Page fetching checks destinations and redirects for non-public addresses and follows robots.txt (RFC 9309). It does not accept arbitrary URLs through MCP. Treat all returned web text as untrusted content.

Use accept language , for example "ko-KR,ko;q=0.9,en;q=0.8" , to request a page-language preference in MCP read page or HTTP include raw content . Omission sends no language header; each preference has its own cached page. See validation, providers, and pagination.

For page text, include raw content=1 uses the HTTP API. PDF text extraction requires Poppler ( pdftotext ); scanned PDFs require a separate OCR tool. JavaScript-rendered pages need the optional Firefox renderer. Neither is enabled automatically by a standalone release binary.

With include raw content=1 , every result reports raw content status ( ok , not requested , too large , fetch failed , robots blocked , extract failed , render failed , or unknown ) and, where available, a short raw content error message, so a client can decide whether to retry or give up from the response alone. The page body limit is configurable through raw content max bytes (default 4 MiB, bounded at 32 MiB), and a failed page renderer keeps the static text by default ( page renderer fallback = "static" ).

 Search profiles

Choose a provider configuration with --profile . The default is standard .

Standard's shipped entries are documented APIs, RSS or JSON endpoints — no human-facing search-result HTML pages are fetched by default — and each entry's reviewed conditions are recorded in docs/PROVIDERS.md. Full adds HTML providers, including sources whose terms forbid automated access; starting it now prints a terms reminder at startup.

 Profile Command Sources 
 --- --- --- 
 Standard rustxng 34 keyless entries with recorded endpoint/use conditions, plus local indexes 
 Clean rustxng --profile clean Search only prebuilt local crawl and Wikipedia-dump indexes; no external search-provider requests 
 Full rustxng --profile full Additional HTML providers, including sources with restrictive or unverified automation terms, plus billed Exa Search (skipped at startup when EXA API KEY is absent) 

 Full is not a permission bypass. Do not enable a provider without the permissions required for your use. A private instance does not override provider terms. Clean is a configuration choice, not a certification of legal compliance.

The selected profile also works with MCP, for example rustxng mcp --profile clean . Standard and Full send queries to their enabled external providers even when RustXNG runs locally. Clean searches local indexes only, but explicitly requested raw page fetching or other network-backed features can still make outbound requests. Full's Exa integration is opt-in and billed; an API key alone does not enable Exa in Standard.

Standard excludes unreviewed providers from its defaults. Reviews apply to the documented retrieval scope, not every commercial use, content licence, storage policy or redistribution scenario. See provider conditions and dated measurements.

 Installation and configuration

A Docker image is available:

 

By default, the service binds to loopback. Exposing it to another network requires appropriate access controls. The process stops cleanly on SIGTERM or Ctrl-C: in-flight requests finish before it exits, so docker stop and systemctl stop do not have to kill it.

install.html:
Install from the releases page or with Cargo. Release binaries are available for Linux, macOS and Windows; check the matching asset and its SHA-256 sidecar before running it.

cargo install --git https://github.com/sahenjp/RustXNG.git --tag v0.32.0 --locked

Rust 1.89 or newer and a C build toolchain are required for source installation. The agent setup guide covers release binaries, verification, platform requirements and service reuse.

Start a local server:

rustxng --bind 127.0.0.1 --port 29483

Search from another terminal:

curl --fail --get 'http://127.0.0.1:29483/search' \
  --data-urlencode 'q=tokio runtime documentation' \
  --data 'format=json' --data 'max_results=5'

Results contain a title, URL, snippet and source metadata. For automated clients that need errors for unknown engine names, add strict_engines=1 (the default preserves SearXNG-compatible fallback behavior). Useful optional parameters include language=ja, engines=wikipedia, include_domains=docs.rs, exclude_domains=example.com, time_range=day, and include_raw_content=1. Time filtering depends on provider support.

The web interface is at http://127.0.0.1:29483/. The search endpoint also supports CSV, RSS and HTML output.
